newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen still up at Tokyo noon but off highs.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen still up at Tokyo noon but off highs.

text.p: The key December Euroyen futures contract was higher by midday in Tokyo on Friday but off earlier highs touched partly on buying sentiment carried over from overnight trade.

An overnight media report quoted an unnamed Bank of Japan (BOJ) official as saying that the Japanese economic recovery is not strong enough to sustain an interest rate rise. This prompted buying of both Japanese government bonds (JGBs) and Euroyen futures, traders said.
The key December contract ended the morning at 98.88 after moving from 98.88 to 98.91, with 54,486 contracts traded.
Key December settled at 98.86 on Thursday.
In the late morning, the ruling Liberal Democratic Party's (LDP) administrative reform panel said it will recommend that the Japanese government raise interest rates in the future.
An official told Reuters: "People are having a hard time as a result of low interest rates...We would like to call on the government to show more consideration to this situation."
No impact on Euroyen futures was detected, but a city bank dealer said this could weigh the market down in the afternoon.
A trader at a securities firm said the topside was growing heavy around the technical resistance point of 98.91-92.
"A fairly good volume of offers is lined up here. But should December manage to break above this point, rises to 98.99 and above are possible," he added.

In the interbank market, key overnight call money was being traded at around 0.50 percent, up from 0.49 percent on Thursday, despite an accommodative BOJ money market operation. Traders attributed this to strong fund-raising demand ahead of the end of the month.
The BOJ injected a net 100 billion yen into the market against a net shortfall of 10 billion yen, in line with market expectations.
